contribution.value: Introduces LLM-KICK, a knowledge-intensive benchmark that re-evaluates SoTA pruning and quantization methods beyond perplexity, showing pruning fails at modest sparsity while quantization is more successful but still drops on knowledge tasks.

ev.quote: We introduce Knowledge-Intensive Compressed LLM BenchmarK (LLM-KICK), a collection of carefully curated tasks to redefine the evaluation protocol for compressed LLMs
We use FreebaseQA (Jiang et al., 2019) which is a dataset for open-domain QA over the Freebase knowledge graph
We use the popular MMLU (Massive Multitask Language Understanding) benchmark which covers 50+ subjects across STEM, Humanities, Social Sciences, and more
We use TriviaQA (Joshi et al., 2017) for evaluation, a popular reading comprehension dataset which includes 95K question-answer pairs
We use a popular summarization dataset CNN/DailyMail (Chen et al., 2016) for evaluation

ev.section: A.1.2 QUANTIZATION IN LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS
ev.quote: GPTQ (Frantar et al., 2022) proposes a novel layer-wise quantization technique based on approximate second-order information resulting a bitwidth reduction to 3 or 4 bits per weight
several works have shown significant success in *training-free* and *data-free* compression (pruning and quantization) of LLMs

strengths.value: First holistic benchmark (LLM-KICK) that exposes how perplexity hides large knowledge losses in compressed LLMs across factoid QA, reasoning, retrieval, summarization, and instruction following.

ev.quote: LLM-KICK is designed to holistically access compressed LLMs' ability for language understanding, reasoning, generation, in-context retrieval, in-context summarization, etc.

strengths.value: Compares four leading methods (Magnitude, SparseGPT, Wanda, GPTQ) plus AWQ and LLM.int8 across three model scales (7B, 13B, 33B) and two model families (Vicuna, LLaMA-2).

ev.section: 3 LLM-KICK: Unveiling True Merits of LLM Compression
ev.quote: our work primarily focuses on the top-2 existing training-free and data-free LLM pruning techniques (i.e., SparseGPT (Frantar & Alistarh, 2023) and Wanda (Sun et al., 2023)), along with the baseline of One-shot Magnitude-based Pruning (Han et al., 2016), plus a popular quantization technique (GPTQ)

strengths.value: Shows quantization preserves knowledge much better than pruning, while pruning still works for in-context retrieval and summarization at high sparsity.

ev.quote: current quantization methods are more successful than pruning; yet, pruned LLMs even at ≥ 50% sparsity are robust in-context retrieval and summarization systems

strengths.value: Reproducible: averages 3 independent runs per cell and releases code at github.com/VITA-Group/llm-kick.

ev.quote: The reproduced codes are available at https://github.com/VITA-Group/llm-kick

weaknesses.value: Evaluation restricted to Vicuna decoder-only models due to license; limits generality across architectures.

ev.quote: We primarily restrict our evaluation to Vicuna (decoder-only architecture) due to its open-source license, high performance, and instruction-following ability

weaknesses.value: Does not test parameter-efficient recovery; future work to use LoRA/QLoRA is acknowledged but not done.

ev.quote: For future work, we aim to investigate how the lost knowledge due to compression can be recovered using parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods, e.g., LoRA

weaknesses.value: GPT-4 is the judge for summarization and instruction following, which adds dependence on a closed proprietary scorer.
